tldr: Appendix C presents survey responses from diverse Oregon stakeholders on competitiveness and prosperity. Dominant concerns: natural gas workers oppose the Oregon Climate Protection Program (CPP), citing threats to family-wage jobs and rising energy costs; others advocate for education investment, affordable workforce housing, transit infrastructure, living wages, and healthcare. Business-climate respondents criticize anti-business environment and high taxes; rural stakeholders highlight importance of hunting and tourism.

bullets.text: Natural gas industry workers across multiple submissions report CPP increases compliance costs on utilities, forcing companies to reduce projects and cut work hours for union employees.
Jeff Lewis (97321) reports electricity costs doubled in 7 years, from 7 cents/kWh to 14 cents/kWh, with monthly power bills ranging $300–450.
Tyler Brown (97814, Barley Brown's Beer) cites deteriorating interstate gateway infrastructure (e.g., Baker City Exit 304, unchanged since 1970s) as harming Oregon's tourism and visitor economy.

Richard Sheperd (97202) identifies workforce housing shortage as core barrier to economic development and proposes Universal Building Exemption (constitutional amendment), Land Value Capture (6% property tax from transit corridors), and split-roll property tax.
Education advocates call for free/public preschool and college, living wages, and universal healthcare; multiple respondents cite homelessness and food insecurity as urgent priorities.
Business-climate respondents characterize Oregon as anti-business environment with tax rates higher than competing states and excessive regulatory burden.
Kory (97004, Dirty Cowgirl Saloon, Wasco) warns that PEACE Act IP28 hunting ban would devastate rural business; hunters essential to seasonal survival of rural hospitality businesses.
Twila Jacobsen (97405) expresses concern about private equity takeover of healthcare (PeaceHealth/Apollo MD) and advocates for State Bank, fair taxation, and protected public services.
